content.intro: In this lesson, you will study generic methods with a short explanation, an original visual map, a Java example, and a check you can perform yourself. Focus on the relationship between the rule and the behavior rather than memorizing isolated syntax.
content.why_it_matters: This concept matters because it helps you express type relationships so the compiler can prevent invalid combinations. In this lesson, focus on declaring type parameters on methods and use a minimal example to check what the rule actually guarantees.

items.title: Declaring type parameters on methods
items.text: A method gives a named contract to a unit of behavior. Keep responsibilities focused, define clear parameter and return types, and test typical, boundary, and invalid cases independently.

items.title: Type inference
items.text: Generics express relationships between types so the compiler can catch many mistakes before runtime. Bounds and wildcards express different constraints; type erasure means generic type arguments are not generally reified at runtime. Apply that reasoning specifically to type inference and confirm the result with the example or a targeted test.
